target_customer: Software companies and developers who want to automate invoicing and accounts receivable through an API
problem: Companies handle invoicing, reminders and reconciliation manually. Paid offered an API to create and issue invoices, track payments and chase overdue accounts with about 30 minutes of integration.
business_model: Usage-based API priced on the revenue tracked or invoiced, per the Show HN thread

founders.name: Ryan Jackson
previous_startups: A failed earlier YC startup, per a Hacker News comment (unverified)
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as the only founder; he posted the Show HN as ryanwjackson.

exit.reason: CB Insights lists the company as Acquired with no acquirer or date; unverified and possibly a different Paid.

competitors.name: Zuora
competitors.what: Subscription billing platform for larger companies

competitors.name: BillForward
competitors.what: Subscription billing described as Stripe for subscription billing, a YC company presenting at Demo Day
competitors.traction_then: Raising a seed after Demo Day
competitors.funding_then: Seed in progress, amount not stated

technical_complexity.rationale: A billing API with webhooks, payment processor integration (Stripe) and reconciliation is standard fintech engineering with correctness requirements.

defensibility.rationale: Billing integrations lock customers in once embedded, but a Hacker News commenter noted it was just an invoicing program missing hard cases such as EDI and partial deliveries.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe later added Invoicing and Billing products. Whether Paid was acquired is unverified.

market_need_then: Developers wanted API first billing, shown by BillForward's pitch as Stripe for subscription billing in August 2014. The Show HN thread had 88 points and 36 comments, with users asking about Xero integration and check payments.

branding.domain_note: Show HN linked paidapi.com; YC lists paidlabs.com. Neither is an exact match for the plain word.
branding.community_and_virality: Show HN with 88 points and a Product Hunt launch dated March 12, 2015. Later products named Paid or JustPaid confuse searches.

brand_strength.rationale: A short outcome name that says what the product does, but extremely generic and shared by later unrelated billing products.

pivots.from: An earlier YC startup by the founder
pivots.why: A Hacker News commenter says Paid was a pivot from a failed YC startup; no date or reason given

outcome_analysis: Paid launched an invoicing API in 2014 and showed it on Hacker News in early 2015. Aggregator data suggests a small YC investment plus a seed of about 1.4 million dollars in 2015 from Founder Collective, Pear and Squares Capital, and CB Insights marks it as acquired without details. YC lists it inactive. No source explains the end, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: All three rounds rest on a single database, Seedtable, seen only in a search snippet because the page returned 403. The 2014-10 and 2015-10 rounds both show 1.4M and may be one event double counted; the 2014-10 investor is unclear. CB Insights lists about 20K raised and an Acquired stage, which conflicts with Seedtable and may mix in a different Paid (a newer AI billing company and JustPaid also appear). Competitor sources are dated August 2014 and describe BillForward, Zuora and Recurly (Chargify not named in the source). The Show HN date is not shown on the page; it is about early 2015 by its id, so it is not used as a competitor source. The paidlabs.com site returned HTTP 503 so it is treated as unreachable.
